subject: Tenant Data Lifecycle — Hosted API Q&A

Subject: Questions on residency / retention / deletion for Hosted API

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security and legal teams around data residency and lifecycle for the Hosted API:

- Can you confirm whether tenant request/response content is stored outside the US (we need US-only residency)?
- What exactly is retained in logs/telemetry (request payloads, completions, embeddings, debug traces)?
- Backups/snapshots: are they geo-redundant and if so, can they be restricted to a US-only footprint?
- What is your standard retention window for request logs and audit trails? Is that configurable per contract?
- If MedArc requests deletion of a tenant's historical data, what's the process and expected timeline? Will you provide evidence/certificate of deletion?

We handle PHI in some workflows, so clarity here is critical for our compliance team. Attaching our internal checklist would be helpful but wanted your high-level answers first.

Thanks —
Samir
Head of Security, MedArc Systems

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <samir.joshi@medarc.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, legal@medarc.com
Date: 2027-06-01T13:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on residency / retention / deletion for Hosted API

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a short SOC 2 summary and our tenant data flow diagram for reference (SOC2-summary.pdf, tenant-data-flow.png). Happy to walk through any line items on a call.

1) Residency: We support region pinning for hosted tenants. For MedArc we can enable a US-only tenant region (us-west-2 or us-east-1). All primary model serving, logs, and backups for a US-pinned tenant are kept in that region (customer can choose). We do not route tenant-level prompts or completions outside contracted region for pinned tenants.

2) What we retain: by default we keep: 1) request and response metadata (timestamps, model used, token counts) and 2) optional request payloads/completions if the account enables full-text logging (off by default at signup). Embeddings produced and stored in Redwood-managed vectors are retained only if the customer opts-in to persistent embeddings; otherwise they are ephemeral and not written to long-term store. Debug traces and internal performance telemetry are aggregated and scrubbed; raw text traces are not retained long-term unless explicitly enabled for troubleshooting.

3) Backups / snapshots: Backups are encrypted at rest and may be geo-redundant within the US region boundary (we can contractually restrict cross-region replication to within US regions only). For enterprise contracts we can disable cross-region replication altogether and keep backups single-region.

4) Retention windows: default hosted retention is 30 days for request payloads (if logging enabled) and 90 days for audit logs/trace metadata. We offer contract-level retention overrides from 0 days (ephemeral) up to 3 years for audit logs. We document retention windows in the contract and in the Console under Account -> Data Settings.

5) Deletion process & evidence: Deletion requests are handled via our support + compliance workflow. Steps:
   - Customer submits a deletion request (support ticket or API call).
   - We initiate an asynchronous purge job that removes tenant data from primary stores, caches, and index/embeddings.
   - Snapshot windows: if data exists in recent backups, we either remove the tenant snapshot or mark it for redaction depending on the backup retention policy; for enterprise customers we perform explicit snapshot deletion.
   - We provide a deletion job ID and an audit entry that traces the operations performed (timestamp, systems touched). Typical completion: 24–72 hours for primary stores; up to 7 days if snapshot deletion and multi-stage retention are required.

Evidence provided: a signed deletion confirmation (job ID + audit log excerpt) and a short attestation letter on Redwood letterhead if required.

Notes / next steps: please confirm whether you need (A) US-only region enforcement, (B) no persistent embeddings, and (C) a shorter audit-log retention than our default. I can loop in our engineering ops contact for the detailed backup/snapshot plan once you confirm.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on residency / retention / deletion for Hosted API

Hi all — adding a few technical details to Evelyn's overview so your infra team has clarity:

- Prompt/response storage: when full-text logging is enabled the transcripts are written to a region-scoped object store (S3) encrypted with a customer-specific CMK if you choose Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK). If logging is disabled, transcripts are never persisted beyond the in-memory serving pipeline and short-term KV caches (~minutes).

- KV cache & prefix caching: these are local to the serving cluster and are evicted on a TTL; they are not part of long-term backups. Deletion jobs explicitly clear caches, invalidate cache keys, and delete persisted objects/indices.

- Embeddings: persistent embeddings are stored in a managed vector DB. Deletion triggers both a logical delete (index removal) and a background compaction job to free space. We include the compaction job ID in the audit trail.

- Backups: nightly snapshots are taken; for enterprise US-only tenants we configure snapshot retention to avoid cross-region replication. Snapshot deletion is asynchronous and may take up to a few days when we need to reconcile with immutable retention windows (e.g., legal hold).

- Deletion proof: our system emits an audit record per subsystem (object store, vector DB, search index, cache invalidation) with a canonical job ID. You can reference that job ID in your internal compliance tracking.

Links: internal runbook for deletion (redwood-internal://runbooks/data-purge) and a public-facing KB I can send if useful — let me know and I'll drop it into the ticket.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
